Effects_AbsModePerTickOneClickPer: Per tick (one click per ABS pump)
Effects_AbsUnsupportedBadge_Tip: Forza Horizon's Data Out telemetry doesn't include ABS pump activity, so this effect will stay silent in FH4/FH5/FH6 regardless of the values you set here.
Effects_AdvancedDuckingOnlyDucksEffectsT: Only ducks effects that overlap in frequency.
Effects_AirborneCutsVibrationsWhileThe: Cuts vibrations while the car is in the air, so a jump feels weightless. Works in Assetto Corsa, Forza, and Farming Simulator (with the TF4ALL Enhanced Telemetry mod), and does nothing in other games.
Effects_AirborneEnabled_Tip: Everything comes back the moment you land. The checkboxes below choose which effects are cut; the engine keeps pulsing by default, since it's still revving.
Effects_AirborneReduction_Tip: How far to turn the chosen effects down while airborne. 100% = fully silent; lower values just dial them back.
Effects_AudioEnabled_Tip: Turns the game's sound (engine, tires, impacts) into wheel vibration. Works even when a game sends no useful telemetry.
Effects_AxleSlipFeelWhichAxleIsSlipping: Feel which axle is slipping: a high scrub texture as the front washes wide, a deep pulse as the rear steps out. The louder axle is the one losing grip. Needs per-tire telemetry (Forza, Assetto Corsa, and Farming Simulator with the TF4ALL Enhanced Telemetry mod).
Effects_AxleSlipFrontPitchHz_Tip: Center of the front scrub tone (default 200). Lower = smoother rub, higher = sharper hiss. The tone still climbs as the front tires reach the limit.
Effects_AxleSlipFrontStrength_Tip: Volume of the high front scrub voice, under the main gain.
Effects_AxleSlipOnsetThreshold_Tip: How close to the grip limit before the voices start speaking. 0.85 = 85% of the limit; lower = earlier warning.
Effects_AxleSlipPredictive_Tip: Predicts the slide from how fast grip is being used up, so the warning arrives a fraction before the limit instead of at it.
Effects_AxleSlipRearPitchHz_Tip: Center of the rear thump (default 35). Lower = heavier, slower thud. Also the floor for the wheelspin-locked pulse.
Effects_AxleSlipRearStrength_Tip: Volume of the deep rear pulse voice, under the main gain.
Effects_AxleSlipRevLocked_Tip: The rear pulse speeds up and slows down with the spinning wheels themselves, so wheelspin feels like wheels turning rather than a generic buzz.
Effects_AxleSlipUndersteerJudder_Tip: Depth of the grip-slip-grip chatter once the front is past the limit. 0 = smooth scrub only.
Effects_BumpsLeadingEdge_Tip: The extra whack the instant a wheel first strikes a hard bump: ruts, edges, drops. 0 = smooth texture only.
Effects_BumpsSurfaceEnabled_Tip: Forza-only: drives a second oscillator from the per-tire SurfaceRumble channel. Continuous road feel that's stronger on dirt/grass and lighter on asphalt. Curb thump handles the hit when a wheel first finds a curb.
Effects_BumpsSurfaceRumbleScale_Tip: Multiplier on Forza's SurfaceRumble before driving the oscillator. 1.0 = use as-is. Bump up for more aggressive surface feel.
Effects_CaptureExeOverride_Tip: Saved per-game and applied within 1 second.
Effects_CaptureNotWorkingAudioCaptureNot: Audio capture not picking up your game?
Effects_CaptureNotWorkingTypeTheGameSExe: Type the game's exe name here (with or without ".exe").
Effects_CollisionAThudOnImpactThat: A thud on impact that hits harder the bigger the crash.
Effects_CollisionEnabled_Tip: Project CARS 2 supplies its native impact magnitude; other games derive it from sudden acceleration spikes above about 5g, well above hard cornering or curbs.
Effects_CollisionMaxAmplitude_Tip: Cap on the loudest hit. Safety knob for wrists / wheelbase.
Effects_CollisionMinThreshold_Tip: Lower = lighter contacts trigger. Raise if light scrapes are too noisy.
Effects_CollisionWaveform_Tip: Shape of the impact thud. Square is the punchiest; Sine is softer.
Effects_DrsAQuickChirpTheMoment: A quick chirp the moment DRS opens, then a faint sustained tone while the wing stays open. Silent on games that don't expose DRS.
Effects_DrsActivationWaveform_Tip: Shape of the brief blip on the rising edge.
Effects_DrsSustainedToneWhileDrs: Sustained tone (while DRS held open). Set amp to 0 for chirp-only mode.
Effects_DrsSustainedWaveform_Tip: Shape of the held trail. Independent from the activation chirp so a sharp Square blip can have a softer Sine trail.
Effects_DuckFrequencyAware_Tip: Grip textures always win their band, so a slide stays crisp through the engine pulse instead of blending into it.
Effects_DuckingWhenTransientEffectsGear: When transient effects (gear shift, ABS, road bumps, traction loss) fire, continuous effects (engine pulse, audio capture) duck to make room.
Effects_EffectsReportIssue_Tip: Opens a new GitHub issue. Pre-fills your plugin version and active game, and offers to bundle logs.
Effects_EngineElectricCars_Tip: What Engine pulse does for electric cars (detected as electric, or set to Electric in Car facts). Most users prefer the muted hum since real EVs aren't silent (many pump synthetic engine sound). Pick Silent if you want true silence on EVs.
Effects_EngineEnabled_Tip: The engine's firing pulse through the wheel, rising with RPM.
Effects_EngineHighRpmBoost_Tip: Extra engine-pulse strength that ramps in above 50% RPM, so high revs stay strong in the wheel instead of fading.
Effects_EngineLoadLayer_Tip: Adds a low-frequency oscillation at the engine's cycle rate (RPM/120 Hz) alongside the firing pulse. Sits in the band the wheel actually moves at, so the engine keeps feeling present as the firing pulse rolls off at high RPM.
Effects_EngineLowpassHz_Tip: 0 = disabled. Lowers buzzy harmonics on Square/Saw without changing pitch.
Effects_EngineSetTheEngineType: Set the engine type in Car facts (active car card) for the most accurate pulse.
Effects_ImplementThudHumFrequencyHz_Tip: The pump's pitch. Sits above the thud's knock so the two read as one mechanism.
Effects_ImplementThudHydraulicHum_Tip: A pump whine while the linkage or a fold is actually traveling; the thud then lands when the motion settles. 0 = thud only.
Effects_ImplementThudOctaveLayer_Tip: A higher second tone inside the whine so it reads as machinery, not a pure hum. 0 = single tone.
Effects_ImplementThudPitchBend_Tip: How far the whine spools up from below its pitch as motion starts, and again as it settles. 0 = flat pitch.
Effects_ImplementThudRaiseAmount_Tip: How hard lifting OUT of work lands, relative to dropping in. 0 = raising is silent.
Effects_ImplementThudSpeedPitch_Tip: How much a fast-moving linkage raises the whine's pitch.
Effects_ImplementThudSpeedVolume_Tip: How much slow hydraulic movement quiets the whine: it swells as motion picks up and fades as it eases into the stop. 0 = constant loudness.
Effects_ImplementThud_Tip: A mechanical clunk in the wheel when equipment drops into work or lifts back out, the linkage landing and releasing. Lowering lands harder than raising.
Effects_KerbThumpASingleFirmWhack: A single firm whack the instant a wheel first touches a curb, distinct from the rumble that follows. Scales with speed. Needs curb telemetry (Forza games today).
Effects_KerbThumpFrequencyHz_Tip: Lower = deeper whack. 30 Hz default keeps it below the gear-shift thud.
Effects_LockupJudderAFlatSpotPulseWhile: A flat-spot pulse while a braking tire is locked, slowing with the car the way a real flat spot would. Needs per-tire telemetry (Forza and Assetto Corsa today).
Effects_MasterGain_Tip: Overall strength of the plugin's effects. Doesn't change the game's own force feedback.
Effects_PitLimiterActiveAmp_Tip: Peak amplitude while the limiter is engaged.
Effects_PitLimiterFeelsLikeTheEngine: Feels like the engine being cut at low RPM while the pit limiter is engaged: a steady pulse train you can't miss. Works in most racing sims that have a pit lane.
Effects_PitLimiterFrequencyHz_Tip: Tone within each pulse. Lower = deeper thud; higher = brighter.
Effects_PitLimiterPulseLength_Tip: How much of each pulse is filled with sound. Higher = more sustained; lower = more punctuated.
Effects_PitLimiterPulseRateHz_Tip: How fast the pulse opens / closes. 5-10 Hz feels like a real pit limiter cadence.
Effects_RedlineGuessBadgeTheBuzzIsFiring: The buzz is firing at 85% of max RPM because no one has confirmed the real redline start yet (where the tachometer turns red). Set it so the shift cue lands right.
Effects_RevLimiterAHardBuzzWhenYou: A hard buzz when you enter the redline start: an unmistakable shift cue. If it fires at the wrong RPM, fix the redline start in Car facts.
Effects_RevLimiterFrequencyHz_Tip: Tone within each pulse. Higher reads as a more urgent buzz.
Effects_RevLimiterOffsetRowRedlineOffset: Shift the engage point relative to the car's redline. Negative fires the buzz before the redline (an early shift cue); positive fires it after. 0 = right at the redline.
Effects_RevLimiterPulseLength_Tip: How much of each pulse is filled with sound. Higher = more sustained; lower = more punctuated.
Effects_RevLimiterPulseRateHz_Tip: How fast the buzz stutters. Faster feels like an aggressive soft-cut limiter.
Effects_SomethingFeelBrokenOr: Something feel broken or just off?
Effects_TractionNoiseHpRowNoiseHighpassH: Cut sub-audible drift / DC thump from noise. 0 disables.
Effects_TractionNoiseLpRowNoiseLowpassHz: Cut high frequencies from noise. Lower = smoother rumble, higher = grittier.
Effects_TrueforceEqAddBand_Tip: Adds a flat bell at 100 Hz. Drag it where the rattle is.
Effects_TrueforceEqAudition_Tip: Plays a 1.5 s tone at the selected point's frequency through the EQ, so you can feel the resonance and whether the cut tames it. Click a point first.
Effects_TrueforceEqCurveHost_Tip: Arrow keys nudge the selected point, Shift for bigger steps. Alt + drag changes a bell's width. Delete removes the point. Ctrl+Z undoes. The blue bars are the live spectrum of what the wheel gets; the pale line is before the EQ.
Effects_TrueforceEqEnabled_Tip: Boost or cut the plugin's vibration at specific frequencies. Pull a band down where your wheel or rig rings or rattles.
Effects_TrueforceEqReset_Tip: Back to the six flat bands.
Effects_TrueforceEqTamesTheFrequenciesTh: Tames the frequencies that make your wheel or rig rattle, or lifts the ones it barely renders. Applies in every game and preset. Drag a point to move it, scroll on it for width, double-click to add a band, right-click to remove one.
Effects_TrueforceEqUndo_Tip: Undo the last change to the curve. Ctrl+Z in the graph does the same.
EngineEditor_ElectricConvertNote: This engine was saved as electric. Saving here converts it to a firing-pattern engine. For electric cars, use the built-in Electric engine type and the EV behavior setting instead.
EngineEditor_FiringPattern_Tip: Picks how pulses distribute within one 720° engine cycle. Even-fire covers Inline / Boxer / V60° / V90° / V8 flat-plane / V10 / V12 / W12-16 / V4.
EngineEditor_NameText_Tip: What this engine is called in the Engine dropdowns, e.g. 'LS3 swap' or 'Crossplane R1'.
EngineEditor_PatternHelp: Each number is when a cylinder fires within one engine cycle, from 0 to 1.
EngineEditor_Pattern_Tip: Comma-separated positions from 0 up to (but not including) 1, marking where each pulse fires within one engine cycle. Optional ':amplitude' suffix per pulse (0.25:0.85) makes that pulse softer. Auto-fills when you pick a shape / count above; hand-edit for odd-fire engines.
EngineEditor_PickTheFiringPattern: Pick the firing pattern closest to the real engine and set the cylinder or rotor count. Save, then choose your new engine in a variant's Engine dropdown to hear it on that car.
EngineEditor_RegeneratePattern_Tip: Rebuild the pattern from the shape and cylinder count above. Replaces any manual edits.
EngineEditor_ShapeEvenFireCylCount: Even-fire (cyl count picks Inline / Boxer / V / W)

Replugging the wheel or moving it to a different USB port can also bring it back. If that doesn't fix it, please use Report an issue with a log attached.

Lightsync_AlwaysRememberPattern: Remember my pick for each car automatically
Lightsync_AlwaysRememberPattern_Tip: Off by default, so flicking through patterns to look at them does not pin whichever one you stopped on.
Lightsync_GivesYourWheelThe: Gives your wheel the car's own colors and fill direction as you get in it, lighting each LED at the RPM the real car does.
Lightsync_LedTrimB_Tip: Show white, then bring this down until the strip looks neutral rather than tinted.
Lightsync_LedTrimG_Tip: Show yellow, then bring this down until it stops looking green.
Lightsync_LedTrimOnlyTheGapBetween: Only the gap between the sliders matters. The highest one is the reference and keeps its color as authored; the others are cut relative to it. Three equal sliders means no correction at all, whatever the number.
Lightsync_LedTrimR_Tip: Normally left at 100. Red is usually the dimmest of the three, so there is nothing to gain by cutting it further.
Lightsync_LedTrimReset_Tip: Put the trim back to the tuning this wheel ships with.
Lightsync_LedTrimWhite_Tip: Light all ten in plain white. Hold a sheet of paper next to it and trim until they agree.
Lightsync_LedTrimYellow_Tip: Light all ten in plain yellow, the color that shows a green imbalance most clearly.
Lightsync_LedTrimYourWheelSLEDsAre: Your wheel's LEDs are not equally bright per color, and this makes up the difference. Yellow looking green? Bring green down. White looking blue? Bring blue down. Judge it on the rim, not on screen, and move in small steps. Set it once and leave it.
Lightsync_LightPatternsPerCar: Light patterns, per-car redlines and blink rates by
Lightsync_LightsyncCycleHintDismiss_Tip: Don't show this again. Rev pattern next is on the Controls tab whenever you want it.
Lightsync_LightsyncCycleTheExtrasAreSwap: The extras are swapped into one slot as you go, so a button press walks the whole library without taking your hands off the wheel. Set that button here and you never need this tab mid-race.
Lightsync_LightsyncCycleYourWheelHoldsFi: Your wheel holds five patterns. This holds as many as you like.
Lightsync_LovelyCarData: Match my wheel to the car I'm driving
Lightsync_LovelyCarData_Tip: Works even in games that light the wheel themselves, because the colors are set once as the car loads and the game drives the lights from there. Needs community features, which is where the car data comes from.
Lightsync_LovelyNeedsCommunityNote: Turn on community features in the Settings tab to use this. The car data is fetched from there.
Lightsync_OpensTheLovelyCar_Tip: Opens the lovely-car-data project on GitHub.
Lightsync_PatternApplyTrim_Tip: On for colors you picked on screen, so they come out on the wheel looking like they do here. Off for a pattern you took off the wheel or tuned by eye on the rim: the tuning is already baked into those colors, and applying it again would shift them.
Lightsync_PatternCopy_Tip: Duplicate this pattern, so a shipped one can be used as a starting point.
Lightsync_PatternDirection_Tip: Which way the lights come up as the revs climb.
Lightsync_PatternFillAll_Tip: Set every LED to the current color.
Lightsync_PatternList_Tip: Double-click a name to rename it. The bracketed ones live on the wheel; the rest are swapped in as needed, so they need SimHub running.
Lightsync_PatternMakerClickAnLedToSelect: Click an LED to select it. Left here is left on the wheel, and the wheel shows the whole pattern while you work.
Lightsync_PatternMakerMakeYourOwnWheel: Make your own wheel light patterns. The wheel only stores five, so Trueforce For All keeps as many as you like and swaps them into one slot you lend it. Bind Rev pattern next on the Controls tab to step through them while you drive.
Lightsync_PatternMakerTheBlueBracketMark: The blue bracket marks what is stored on the wheel itself. Everything below it is swapped in as needed.
Lightsync_PatternMakerUpAndDownDecideWhe: Up and Down decide where a pattern lives. The top five are the wheel's own slots: move one up into them and it goes onto the wheel, move it down and it comes off.
Lightsync_PatternMirror_Tip: Copy the LED you have selected onto the one opposite it, so LED 2 pairs with LED 9. For the fills that work in pairs.
Lightsync_PatternPreview_Tip: Sweeps the strip so you can watch which way it fills.
Lightsync_PatternReset_Tip: Put a shipped pattern back the way it came.
Lightsync_PatternReverse_Tip: Turn the whole strip back to front, so the first LED takes the last one's color. For a ramp built from the wrong end.
Lightsync_PickAPatternWhile: Pick a pattern while you are in a car and it becomes that car's pattern, with no need to press Remember. Only deliberate picks count.
Lightsync_WhatTheDatasetCovers_Tip: What the dataset covers, and what comes from our own car facts.

Settings_ArcadeLadderClimbHelp: Puts the ten times around yours on the shop board, with you fifth, and makes the time to beat the driver just ahead.
Settings_ArcadeLeaderboardOptionsTwoBoar: Two boards, so they can show different things. Your own times are on both. The shop board is also the time to beat the game shows you while driving.

Settings_ArcadeSubmitTimes: Send my finished Time Attack runs to the leaderboard
Settings_ArcadeSubmitTimesHelp: Sent under your Trueforce For All username, so it needs you signed in. Only runs you finish are sent; records already in your save are never uploaded.
Settings_AutoSubmitCarFacts: Share my car data with the community
Settings_AutoSubmitCarFacts_Tip: When on, your redline and engine-type corrections are submitted automatically, and naming a car offers a share prompt. Needs community features on; no account required. Turn off to stop sharing car data.
Settings_AutoSyncBackup_Tip: Automatically uploads your setup to the cloud as you change it, and pulls those changes down on your other signed-in devices. Sign-in required.
Settings_AutoUpdateDownloadedPresets_Tip: When a curator publishes a new version of a preset you downloaded, apply it silently. Only runs when you haven't edited your local copy since download.
Settings_BackupASupporterPerkSupport_Tip: A supporter perk. Support on Patreon (Account tab) to enable cloud backup.
Settings_BackupAskMePromptsOnce: 'Ask me' prompts once per change; you can tick 'remember my choice' on that prompt to stop being asked.
Settings_BackupBacksUpYourSettings: Backs up your settings, presets, defaults, car facts and light patterns. Restore the same setup on another PC by signing in there.
Settings_BackupBundleYourFullSetup: Bundle your full setup into one archive for moving to a new machine. To share individual presets or car tunings, use Import / Export in the Preset Manager instead.
Settings_BackupFfbTuningFromADifferent: FFB tuning from a different wheel model:
Settings_BackupNow_Tip: Upload your current setup to the cloud now.
Settings_BackupOffBackUpOnlyWhen: Off = back up only when you click 'Back up now'.
Settings_BackupSelfTest_Tip: Dev only: runs the backup round-trip + the classification audit (flags any unclassified TrueforceSettings field) and shows the result.
Settings_Backup_Tip: Save settings + every user preset + every default + every car tuning to a single .zip you can carry to another machine.
Settings_BetaUpdates_Tip: Receive pre-release 'beta' builds through the in-app updater, so you can try new effects and fixes before they reach the stable release. Pre-releases are always public on GitHub; this just brings them to the in-app updater. Turn it off to return to the stable release next time one ships.
Settings_CommunityEnabled_Tip: Lets the plugin go online for community features: downloading and submitting community car facts, sharing presets, and fetching per-car rev-light data from the Lovely Sim Racing dataset on GitHub. Turn off to stay offline for community features (already-downloaded community car facts still apply if 'Use community car facts' is on). Does not affect account sign-in or cloud backup.
Settings_CrossWheelFfbApply_Tip: Apply the held-back FFB tuning to this PC anyway.
Settings_CrossWheelFfbDismiss_Tip: Keep this PC's own FFB tuning and discard the held-back tuning.
Settings_CrossWheelFfbMode_Tip: Force feedback tuning (Telemetry Based FFB) is dialed in for a specific wheel. Your FFB always backs up; this controls what happens when a restore or sync brings tuning made for a different wheel model (G PRO, RS50, G923).
Settings_CrossWheelFfbRemember_Tip: Apply this choice to future syncs from a different wheel model without asking again. (Apply anyway = always apply; Dismiss = never apply. Change later under 'FFB tuning from a different wheel model'.)
Settings_DashPhoneSettings: Open on your phone or tablet…
Settings_DashPhoneSettings_Tip: Shows a QR code and link that open TF4ALL Dash on your phone.
Settings_DiagnosticsHelpsDecideWhatTo: Helps decide what to build next. Anonymous.
Settings_DriverIntercept: Driver testing mode: route FFB through the kernel filter driver (claims sole wheel ownership). Experimental.
Settings_DriverInterceptHelp: Restart SimHub or re-detect the wheel after changing this.
Settings_DriverIntercept_Tip: Experimental. Claims sole ownership of the wheel through the TFFA kernel filter driver and routes the game's force feedback through the Trueforce stream. Needs the TFFA filter driver installed. Takes effect on the next plugin start (restart SimHub or re-detect).
Settings_EffectsTabShareButtons: Show preset Share buttons on the active car/game card
Settings_EffectsTabShareButtons_Tip: Adds a Share button to the active game and car on the header card so you can share the preset you're driving. Turn off to keep the Effects tab clean; the Preset Manager is still the place to share. Doesn't affect community car facts.
Settings_ExportLogs_Tip: Zips your SimHub logs + TF4ALL settings to your Desktop. Attach the zip to your GitHub issue so I can debug what's happening on your machine. The zip includes your settings file (username, game list, tuning); skim it before posting it publicly.
Settings_FfbPassthroughForceComesBackAs: Force comes back as soon as the game does. Brief interruptions like an overlay or a notification are ignored.
Settings_FfbPassthroughIfTheWheelMisbeha: If the wheel misbehaves around pauses or fast travel, try flipping this.
Settings_ForzaBind_Tip: Local IP to listen on. 0.0.0.0 = all interfaces (recommended). Use a specific LAN IP only if you want to filter.
Settings_ForzaDiscovery: Forza packets detected on a different port.
Settings_ForzaDiscoveryOnPort_Fmt: Forza packets detected on port {0}. Switch to it?
Settings_ForzaDiscoveryOtherPort: Forza packets detected on a different port. Switch to it?
Settings_ForzaForwardEnabled: Also forward to SimHub (dashboards, ShakeIt / Buttkicker, etc.)
Settings_ForzaForwardEnabled_Tip: Enable when you also use SimHub for Forza (dashboards, ShakeIt bass shakers / Buttkicker, anything SimHub drives). Forza can only send telemetry to one place, so this plugin receives it and relays every packet on to SimHub. Live telemetry passes through unaltered; short replay and menu gaps are filled on the forwarded copy so SimHub does not read them as the game disconnecting.
Settings_ForzaForwardHost_Tip: 127.0.0.1 if SimHub runs on the same PC. A LAN IP (or hostname) for a separate SimHub host.
Settings_ForzaForwardPort_Tip: The port SimHub is listening on for Forza Data Out. Match this to the UDP port shown in SimHub's Forza Game config.
Settings_ForzaForwardStatusArmed: (armed, will relay once a Forza title is detected)
Settings_ForzaPort_Tip: Match this in Forza's DATA OUT IP PORT. Default 5300; pick anything if it collides with another listener (SimHub's typical 4123, Sim Racing Studio's 4123, etc.).
Settings_ForzaSectionForzaAlreadyPointsA: Forza already points at this plugin; this just relays a copy on to SimHub.

Settings_ForzaStatusReceiving_Fmt: Receiving at ~{0} Hz, {1}. {2} packets this session.

Settings_ForzaStatusStalled_Fmt: No packets arriving now (0 Hz). {0} received earlier this session. If you're in-game, check Forza Data Out config + the troubleshooter below.
Settings_ForzaTroubleshootConfirmForzaSD: • Confirm Forza's DATA OUT is ON, and its IP and PORT match this plugin (IP 127.0.0.1, PORT = the Port field above).
Settings_ForzaTroubleshootFirewallWindow: • Firewall: Windows Defender may prompt the first time the listener opens. Allow it on private/domain networks.
Settings_ForzaTroubleshootMostSetupsRece: Most setups receive fine on 127.0.0.1. If you're getting zero packets, work through these:
Settings_ForzaTroubleshootPortCollisionW: • Port collision with SimHub or another tool? Pick a different port here, then update Forza's DATA OUT IP PORT to match.
Settings_ForzaTroubleshootStillNothingOn: • Still nothing on 127.0.0.1: set Forza's DATA OUT IP ADDRESS to your PC's LAN IP (e.g. 192.168.x.x) instead, and leave the bind address here at 0.0.0.0. This gets around localhost quirks on some installs.
Settings_FoundABugWeirdBehavior: Found a bug, weird behavior, or have a feature request? Open an issue on GitHub.
Settings_FsModOptionalPerGameMods: Optional per-game mods that unlock extra features. Install copies the mod into the game's own folders; Remove deletes it again.
Settings_LogUsbBytes: Log raw USB FFB packets to usb-trace.pcap (for support)
Settings_LogUsbBytes_Tip: Off by default. When on, captures every USB OUT transfer to your wheel (any endpoint, any transfer type) as a pcap file alongside SimHub's logs. Open in Wireshark with USBPcap. Use only when support asks for it: the file grows several KB/sec during active FFB. Capped at 50 MB; toggle off and on to reset.
Settings_MotdNoneWarning: With messages off, you may miss important announcements like outage notices or critical fixes.
Settings_NetworkAShortMessageAtThe: A short message at the top of this window: announcements, tips, and the occasional bit of news.
Settings_NetworkIfYouVeChangedYour: If you've changed your local copy, those changes are kept; the curator's update is offered through the updates-available chip instead.
Settings_NetworkPreReleaseTheCommunity: Pre-release: the community backend is in testing. Shared presets, packs, and custom engines are test data and may be reset before the public launch. Your account, achievements, and car data you contribute are kept.
Settings_NetworkSignInIsOnlyNeeded: Sign-in is only needed for presets. Anything you share there (presets, packs, custom engines) shows your username; car facts are anonymous and need no account.
Settings_NetworkSubmissionsAreAnonymousA: Submissions are anonymous and work without an account; signed-in contributions count toward achievements.
Settings_PerfAutoRadio_Tip: Start at smallest ring sizes; ratchet up on persistent dropouts. Survived size is remembered across sessions.
Settings_PerfCounters: Output ring: 0 underruns/min · Audio ring: 0 glitches/min
Settings_PerfCountersDetail_Fmt: Output ring (cap {0}): {1} underruns/min · Audio ring (cap {2}): {3} glitches/min
Settings_PerfManualRadio_Tip: Lock the slider values. No automatic changes. Use for streaming or force-testing.
Settings_PerfReset_Tip: Drop both rings back to the smallest configured value. In Auto mode the ratchet will re-discover whether your machine can hold them.
Settings_PerformanceAudioRing_Tip: Sample buffer between WASAPI loopback and the audio mixer. Runs 16 to 128 samples; 16 is both the smallest and the default. If you hear continuous clicks, raise it, or let the auto-ratchet (Auto mode) raise it for you.
Settings_PerformanceCountersTallyEventsI: Counters tally events in a rolling 60-second window. If they are going up, your machine is glitching at the current ring size.
Settings_PerformanceOutputRing_Tip: Sample buffer between the audio mixer and the USB stream. Smaller = lower wheel latency, but Windows must wake the stream thread on time.
Settings_PerformanceSmallerRingBuffersLe: Smaller ring buffers = less latency between game and wheel, but require Windows to wake our threads on time.
Settings_ReleaseOnFocusLoss: Let go of the wheel when you switch away from the game
Settings_ReleaseOnFocusLoss_Tip: On by default. Alt-tab out of the game and the wheel goes free instead of holding whatever force it had. Some games stop sending force feedback the moment they lose focus without telling anyone, and a held force with no self-aligning torque behind it slowly walks the wheel to full lock. Turn it off if you run the game windowed alongside something else and want force to continue.
Settings_RemoteDashAppliesToTheRevLed: Applies to the rev LED strip on the TF4ALL Dash dashboard. On Auto the strip is your wheel's own strip, drawn on the phone. The other two draw a green to red ramp scaled to the current car's redline, which is also what Auto falls back to when there is no wheel to follow. Either way it flashes in step with the wheel at the redline, and changes apply instantly with no dashboard reload.
Settings_RemoteDashControlEffectsGainsAn: Control effects, gains, and presets from your phone or tablet while driving.
Settings_RemoteDashDefaultTab_Tip: The tab the dash opens on when 'Remember last used tab' is off. Applies at the next SimHub start.
Settings_RemoteDashDriveOneRowRadio_Tip: Just the bottom two boxes, with a bigger gear readout above them.
Settings_RemoteDashDrivePerGame_Tip: Each game keeps its own set of four boxes, and switching games loads the one you last used there. Games report different telemetry, so a layout that fills up in one can be half empty in another.
Settings_RemoteDashDriveTwoRowsRadio_Tip: All four boxes, two above and two below.
Settings_RemoteDashFlags: Show race flags on the dash
Settings_RemoteDashFlags_Tip: A colored band across the top of the dash whenever a flag is out.
Settings_RemoteDashIdle: Show the idle card when no game is running
Settings_RemoteDashIdleDelay_Tip: Only applies while a game IS running: how long the car must sit still before the card takes over from the dashboard. Set it long if you would rather it never interrupted a session. With no game running the card shows straight away regardless.
Settings_RemoteDashIdleFont_Tip: Applies to the name and number on the idle card. The font has to exist on the device showing the dash, so an unknown one quietly falls back to the default.
Settings_RemoteDashIdleNameAbove_Tip: Puts the driver name over the number instead of under it.
Settings_RemoteDashIdle_Tip: Shows an ambient card with your name and number instead of an empty dashboard. It clears the moment a game starts, and the card has its own Exit button.
Settings_RemoteDashIncidents_Tip: Your incident count sits under the speed on the Drive tab. A band across the top of the dash announces each new incident with what it cost (1x, 4x), and the wheel's screen shows it too. iRacing is the only game that publishes a count, so nothing appears anywhere else.
Settings_RemoteDashLapTimesTireAndFuel: Lap times, tire and fuel readouts come from the game, so what they show depends on what that game reports.
Settings_RemoteDashPedals: Show pedals and steering around the gear
Settings_RemoteDashPedals_Tip: Thin throttle and brake bars either side of the gear on the Drive tab, with steering underneath.
Settings_RemoteDashRememberTab_Tip: The dash comes back on whichever tab was open last, surviving SimHub restarts.
Settings_RemoteDashRevCentered: Narrow the rev strip on the Drive tab
Settings_RemoteDashRevCentered_Tip: On the Drive tab only: the strip spans the space above the gear between the two box columns instead of the full width. Other tabs are always full width.
Settings_RemoteDashShowsThePointsYou: Shows the points you have taken against the limit that ends your session, turning violet and then red as you run out of room.
Settings_RemoteDashShowsYellowBlueBlack: Shows yellow, blue, black, white and chequered flags in a band across whichever tab is open. Forza does not report flags, so the band never appears there.
Settings_RemoteDashSpotter: Show the spotter when a car is alongside
Settings_RemoteDashSpotter_Tip: A bar down the edge of whichever tab is open while a car is beside you on that side. Only games that report car positions can drive it; it never appears in the others.
Settings_RemoteDashTheme_Tip: Repaints the dashboard live. Themes change the structural colors only: the greens and reds that mean something keep their meaning.
Settings_RemoteDashUntickATabToHide: Untick a tab to hide it on the dash; use the arrows to change the order. At least one tab always stays on.
Settings_RemoteDashWithThisOnAGameYou: With this on, a game you have not set up yet uses the layout above, and so do changes you make with no game running.
Settings_RemoteRevAutoRadio_Tip: The strip shows your wheel's rev lights: their colors, their fill direction, and the switch-on points of the car you are driving. Falls back to the settings below on a wheel whose lights we cannot read.
Settings_RemoteRevLtrRadio_Tip: The rev strip fills from the left edge toward the right as revs climb.
Settings_RemoteRevOutsideInRadio_Tip: The rev strip lights from both ends toward the center as revs climb.
Settings_ReportIssue_Tip: Opens a new GitHub issue. Pre-fills plugin version and active game so you don't have to type it.
Settings_ResetNotices_Tip: Reset the pop-ups that only show once or were dismissed with 'Don't show again' (welcome, what's new, the iRacing Trueforce notice, the stepped-aside notice for every game, share prompt) so they can appear again.
Settings_RestoreFromCloud_Tip: Download your cloud backup and apply it to this PC (your local-only presets are kept).
Settings_Restore_Tip: Replace all current Trueforce For All settings, presets, defaults, and car tunings with a backup archive's contents. Destructive: confirm before running.
Settings_RpmLedSectionInIRacingYouDisabl: In iRacing you disable native Trueforce, which also switches the wheel's rev lights off. Click Test to check the plugin can light them up.
Settings_SelfTest_Tip: Checks USBPcap, the wheel, stream, FFB pass-through and telemetry (and whether G HUB is open, since it can hold the wheel), then sends a short test buzz so you can confirm the wheel responds.
Settings_ShareUsageStats_Tip: Sends an anonymous once-a-day report (a random id not tied to you or your hardware, the plugin version, your wheel model, the games you play, your settings, and two-letter codes for your Windows display and regional-format languages) so development can follow real use. Never sends your name, account, or anything you type; your IP address is not stored. Turn off to send nothing.

Settings_ShowFeedbackBox_Tip: Adds a TF4ALL master + audio gain box to SimHub's home 'Feedback' section, next to Motors and Wind, for quick access without opening this panel.
Settings_ShowPerGearRedlineEditor: Show per-gear redlines in the Car facts panel
Settings_ShowPerGearRedlineEditor_Tip: Shows the per-gear redline editor in the Car facts panel, for cars where you shift at a different point in specific gears. Cars whose current engine already has per-gear redlines saved keep showing the editor, and saved values keep working either way.
Settings_StopStreamOnPause: Hand the wheel back to the game while paused
Settings_StopStreamOnPause_Tip: Off by default. Turn it on and, when the game pauses (menu, fast travel, race start), the plugin steps fully out of the way, so the wheel uses the game's own force feedback and auto-center. Leave it off and the plugin keeps hold of the wheel while paused. It only bites where the game's own force feedback is what the wheel would fall back to, so it does nothing while the plugin is building or carrying the whole steering force.
Settings_UpdateCheckInterval_Tip: How often the plugin checks GitHub for a newer release while it's running. A check always runs once when SimHub starts, and the header's 'Check for updates' link checks on demand, no matter what you pick here. 'On startup only' just turns off the background re-checks.
Settings_UpdatesBetaBuildsGetFixes: Beta builds get fixes and new effects first, but are less tested.
Settings_UpdatesWhenAnUpdateIsAvailable: When an update is available, an 'Update to vX.Y.Z' button appears in the header up top.
Settings_UsbPcapBrowse_Tip: Point at USBPcapCMD.exe if USBPcap is installed somewhere off the default Program Files path.
Settings_UsbPcapPickDevice_Tip: Scan every USBPcap interface and pick your wheel manually. Use this only if auto-discovery genuinely can't find your wheel: a forgotten manual pin can silently break FFB after a replug. Type MANUALPIN in the access code box to reveal this control.
Settings_UsbPcapReinstall_Tip: Run the bundled USBPcap installer (requires admin). Use this if USBPcap was uninstalled or the install is broken.
Settings_UseCommunityCarFacts: Use community car facts (names, engine types, redlines)
Settings_UseCommunityCarFacts_Tip: Apply community-sourced car facts to your cars: human-readable names, engine types, and redlines. Uses a local cache, so it keeps working offline and only refreshes from the server every few days (or when you hit the refresh icon). Turn off to ignore community car facts entirely and use only your own values.
Settings_WidgetsOffByDefaultToKeep: Off by default to keep the Car facts panel small.

TelemetryFfb_ArcadeHoldMs_Tip: How long the steering force and the spring keep acting after the game stops sending them. Rumble and friction set their own and ignore this.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeMinForce_Tip: Raises the quiet forces without touching the loud ones, for a cabinet whose output is too light on a strong wheel.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeSteerHold_Tip: How long the steering force, the spring and the damper keep acting after the cabinet stops sending them. 0 follows Force linger.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningFooter: These take effect straight away, without restarting the game. FFB scale and smoothing are the controls above, and each cabinet keeps its own.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningForceLinger_Tip: How long the steering force and the spring keep acting after the game stops sending them. Rumble and friction set their own and ignore this.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningMillisecondsBuz: Milliseconds, buzz only. 0 plays each cycle as sent; raise it to smooth a stuttery buzz.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningMillisecondsFor: Milliseconds, for the steering force, spring and damper. 50 is what the cabinet commands. Higher keeps weight in the wheel but holds a force the game already cancelled.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningMillisecondsThe: Milliseconds, the game's own setting, written to its FFBPlugin.ini. It is what the game uses when you run it without SimHub. The two holds below override it here.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningPercentLiftsThe: Percent. Lifts the quiet forces, leaves the loud ones alone.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningPercentTheBuzzA: Percent. The buzz and rumble only; the steering force keeps its own strength.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningSteadyForceHold: How long the steering force, the spring and the damper keep acting after the cabinet stops sending them. 0 follows Force linger.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningVibrationHold_T: How long the buzz keeps playing after the cabinet stops sending it. 0 follows the length the game asks for, which is one cycle.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningWaveformStrengt: Scales only the buzz and rumble this cabinet plays. The steering force is left alone, so a wheel set strong enough for the steering can still have a quieter buzz.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeTuningWeakForceLift_T: Raises the quiet forces without touching the loud ones, for a cabinet whose output is too light on a strong wheel.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeVibHold_Tip: How long the buzz keeps playing after the cabinet stops sending it. 0 follows the length the game asks for, which is one cycle.
TelemetryFfb_ArcadeWaveGain_Tip: Scales only the buzz and rumble this cabinet plays. The steering force is left alone, so a wheel set strong enough for the steering can still have a quieter buzz.
TelemetryFfb_FfbInvert: Invert FFB sign (uncheck if forces feel reversed)
TelemetryFfb_FfbInvert_Tip: Flips the direction of the game's force feedback sent to the wheel. On by default. If your wheel pushes the wrong way (e.g. forces feel reversed in RaceRoom), uncheck this.
TelemetryFfb_FfbSmooth_Tip: Smooths the force before it reaches the wheel. Higher = smoother feel but more lag; lower = tighter response. 0 = none, the default.
TelemetryFfb_FsModBanner: Install the TF4ALL Enhanced Telemetry mod for richer force feedback in Farming Simulator.
TelemetryFfb_FsModBannerInstalled: Installed. It loads the next time Farming Simulator starts, so restart the game if it is running now.
TelemetryFfb_FsModBannerNotReaching: The TF4ALL Enhanced Telemetry mod is installed but its data isn't reaching the plugin. Enable it in the game's mod screen when loading your save, or restart Farming Simulator if SimHub restarted while the game was running.
TelemetryFfb_FsModBannerUpdated: The TF4ALL Enhanced Telemetry mod was updated. Restart Farming Simulator to load the new version; until then some newer features stay off.
TelemetryFfb_FxAutoTuneRepeat_Tip: Run the calibration five times from the SAME starting gains and take the median, reporting the spread. More samples tighten the median: the noisier a measurement is, the more it needs them. Successive single runs are not independent (each measures a correction relative to the gains it starts from), so this is the way to tell a repeatable measurement from a noisy one. Takes about five times as long.
TelemetryFfb_FxAutoTune_Tip: Hands-free calibration (about a minute, hands OFF the wheel): bounded self-pulses measure the wheel's native damper, spring and friction against the plugin's renderer and set the gains to match; also measures the real native-vs-stream force scale. Verify by feel afterwards, then Save. Stop cancels.
TelemetryFfb_FxBenchSectionPlayAnEffectT: Play an effect through the wheel's own firmware (native: the reference feel), then the same effect through the plugin's renderer, and tune until they match. The gain belongs to the picked effect, so you can tune one effect, switch to the next, and tune that one without disturbing the first. Native playback needs the wheel free (no game running). Save stores every effect's tuning as the default for future sessions.
TelemetryFfb_FxTestEffect_Tip: The effect to compare. The gain below belongs to whichever effect is picked here, so each one tunes and saves separately.
TelemetryFfb_FxTestEngine_Tip: The identical effect through the plugin's renderer, streamed as Trueforce force: what games feel under the plugin.
TelemetryFfb_FxTestNative_Tip: The wheel's own DirectInput effect with the Trueforce stream fully STOPPED: the wheel exactly as it is without the plugin. The reference feel.
TelemetryFfb_FxTrace_Tip: Records every force tick to a CSV in Documents\TrueforceForAll: the wheel's velocity as the reader measures it, the smoothed velocity the damper actually multiplies, and the force each effect added. Play an effect, turn the wheel through whatever feels wrong, then press again to save. Keeps the last 30 seconds, so a long recording is fine.
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneGain_Tip: Scales the picked effect only: each family (damper, spring, friction, inertia, waveforms, ramp) keeps its own gain, so you can tune one, switch, and tune the next. Live while an engine effect plays. Save tuning stores them all.
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneInertiaAsDamping_Tip: Off (default) renders inertia properly, from how fast the wheel is speeding up. On renders it from how fast the wheel is turning instead, which is how the wheel's own native inertia feels. For A/B against the firmware. The inertia gain means a different thing in each mode, so retune after switching.
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneInertiaCoasts_Tip: On (default) is real inertia: the wheel resists the push, then carries on turning as the stored energy comes back. Off makes it only ever resist, which is what the wheel's own firmware does. Affects inertia only.
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneLpf_Tip: Low-pass on the PICKED condition's rendered output (anti-ringing). Per-effect, like the gain: each condition (damper, spring, friction, inertia) keeps its own, so drop the damper's below ~70 Hz to smooth a grainy damper without touching the rest. Follows the shared filter until you move it; Save tuning keeps it. 0 = off. Waveforms have no condition filter (greyed).
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneResetAll_Tip: Puts every effect's gain, the direction and the filter back to shipped defaults. Live only: Save afterwards to keep it, or reopen SimHub to get your saved tuning back.
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneResetKind_Tip: Puts the picked effect's gain back to its shipped default. The other effects keep their tuning.
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneSave_Tip: Persists every effect's gain plus direction and filter as the defaults for every session (auto-tune and DAMPCAL update gains too; save afterwards to keep them).
TelemetryFfb_FxTuneSign_Tip: Flips the velocity-coupled effects (damper, friction, inertia) if the rendered damper feels like an anti-damper. Springs never flip.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingAdvancedIRacingSends: iRacing sends telemetry 60 times a second, and each update carries six force samples from the physics steps in between. These options choose whether to fill the gaps between updates and how much of that extra detail to use.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingAutoMaxForce_Tip: The number on this button is what the plugin has watched this car produce, plus a margin. Drive a clean lap, then press it to take that number and start watching again from scratch. It stays greyed until the reading has held steady. Same idea as iRacing's own auto button.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingClipWarn: Above this the strongest moments will clip: Auto leaves about 10 percent spare, and past that the top of big corners flattens off instead of building. Fine if you like it, but detail is lost where the car is working hardest.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingGain_Tip: How strong the WHEEL should be. Your overall preference, roughly a percentage of the wheel's total power. It applies to every car; tune an individual car with its peak force instead.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingKerbAmount_Tip: How much of the strike is taken out. 0 leaves it as the sim sent it; 1 flattens it to the cornering load.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingKerbEasesTheJoltOfAC: Eases the jolt of a curb strike and the buzz of a rumble strip. Off the curb, nothing changes.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingKerbHowMuchOfTheStri: How much of the strike is taken out. 0.60 keeps the hit but takes the sting off it.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingKerbSoftening_Tip: How much of the strike is taken out. 0 leaves it as the sim sent it; 1 flattens it to the cornering load.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingKerb_Tip: Softens the jolt of a curb strike and the buzz of a rumble strip, and leaves everything else alone. The sim reports each wheel's suspension speed six times a frame and says when the car is on a strip; the torque samples from those instants are eased toward the cornering load.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingMaxNmDown_Tip: Lower this car's peak force a step, so it leans harder on the wheel.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingMaxNmUp_Tip: Raise this car's peak force a step, so it feels lighter.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingMaxNm_Tip: The peak steering force this car itself produces, in Nm. Not your wheel's rating: it is the car's number, scaled to fit inside your Strength setting. Lower it and this car leans harder on the wheel; raise it and this car feels lighter.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingPeakForce: Nudge it down to make this car feel heavier, up to make it lighter.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingPeakForceRowCarSPeak: The peak steering force this car itself produces, in Nm. Not your wheel's rating: it is the car's number, scaled to fit inside your Strength setting. Lower it and this car leans harder on the wheel; raise it and this car feels lighter.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingSoftLockHowHardTheSt: How hard the stop pushes back. 1.00 is the wheel's full force.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingSoftLockStopStrength: How hard the stop pushes back, as a share of the wheel's full force. 1.00 is a wall; lower lets a determined push through.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingSoftLockStopsTheWhee: Stops the wheel where the car's steering stops.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingSoftLockStrength_Tip: How hard the stop pushes back, as a share of the wheel's full force. 1.00 is a wall; lower lets a determined push through.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingSoftLock_Tip: Stops the wheel where the car's steering stops. The sim normally does this through its own force feedback, which is off while the plugin carries the force, so the plugin renders the stop itself from the sim's steering position and lock.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingTuningStrength_Tip: How strong the WHEEL should be. Your overall preference, roughly a percentage of the wheel's total power. It applies to every car; tune an individual car with its peak force instead.
TelemetryFfb_IRacingTuningTheOnlyForceCo: The only force control you should need day to day. 1.00 delivers what the sim asked for. Raise it if the wheel feels light, lower it if it clips.
TelemetryFfb_IdleLedMode_Tip: What the lights do when nobody is driving: no game running, or a game running with the car sat still past the dash's idle delay.
TelemetryFfb_LedBrightness_Tip: How bright the wheel's lights are, for every pattern. This is the wheel's own setting and it stays where you put it.
TelemetryFfb_LedSweep_Tip: How long one full pass takes, up the strip and back down.
TelemetryFfb_LovelyFill: Use the car's own rev light timing
TelemetryFfb_LovelyFillBlockYourLightsFi: Your lights fill at the RPMs the real car's dash lights up at, instead of an even spread from idle to redline.
TelemetryFfb_LovelyFill_Tip: Needs community features, which is where the car data comes from.
TelemetryFfb_LovelyPerCarRevLightTiming: Per-car rev light timing, redlines and blink rates by
TelemetryFfb_ModeBAutoStrength_Tip: Learns how hard each car pushes the wheel, then scales it to match your Strength setting.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBCenter_Tip: Follows the wheel's own position, so a released wheel settles into center instead of swinging past.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBContentionWarning: The game is still sending its own force feedback, so two force streams are fighting and the wheel will feel jumpy or buzzy. In the game's wheel settings, set force feedback and vibration strength to 0 so this is the only force on the wheel.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBDamper: Resistance to wheel motion. The heavy, planted feel that is not grip force.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBEnabled: Enable Telemetry Based FFB for this game
TelemetryFfb_ModeBEnabled_Tip: Remembered per game, for whichever game is running.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningExtraWeight: Extra weight per g of cornering load. Fast sweepers get heavy, slow hairpins stay light. 0 = off.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningLevelsCarsO: Levels cars out so every car lands at the heaviness your Strength slider sets. The trade: cars stop feeling lighter or heavier than each other. Takes a few laps per car to settle.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningOverallStee: Overall steering force. Your wheel's defaults set the starting point.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2ARele: A released wheel settles instead of oscillating, because the force is led slightly ahead of the wheel to cancel telemetry lag.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2Braki: Braking in a straight line makes almost no force, so the wheel cannot start swinging left and right on its own. Cornering feel is unchanged.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2Caste: Caster-style pull toward straight, scaled up with speed (a parked wheel stays free).
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2FlipT: Flip this if the wheel pulls INTO the slide instead of countering it.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2Force: Force shaping and plumbing. The defaults suit almost everyone.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2HowEa: How early weight arrives. Lower = heavier in normal cornering; 1.0 = force grows linearly to the limit.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2HowFa: How far ahead of the wheel's motion the centering aims. Raise if a released wheel overshoots center; lower if centering feels nervous.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2HowQu: How quickly steering weight returns as the tires regain grip after a lockup or slide. Lower snaps back fast, higher hands the weight back gently.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2Input: Input smoothing. Higher = calmer wheel, slightly laggier response.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2LeadM: Raise the lead only until a released wheel stops ringing; too much adds nervousness on fast transitions.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2OneFr: One front wheel hitting a bump or curb kicks the rim the way a real rack does; both wheels together cancel.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2SoftC: Soft ceiling on the steering force: stacked cornering weight and road kick compress into the top of the range instead of clipping flat.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2Softe: Softens the wheel as you catch a slide back through center, so the moment the force switches sides stops snapping and feeling unstable. Digging deeper into a drift keeps its full weight.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2Steer: Steering weight breathes with real front-axle load: braking dive loads up, crests go light.
Steering weight tops out just before the grip limit and holds, like a real tire; the plateau is your approach warning.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2TheWh: The wheel lightens at each car's real grip limit, learned as you drive (about a lap of pushing). Off = a fixed manual grip limit (the slider below).
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningPanel2Torqu: Torque left once the front has fully let go. Lower = a more dramatic gone-light cue.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBForzaTuningTheSmallest: The smallest force your wheel will play.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGameNote: Enable this per game, for whichever game is running. Set that game's own force feedback and vibration to 0.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGameNoteAppliesTo_Fmt: Applies to {0}. Set that game's own force feedback and vibration to 0.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGameNoteFm8_Fmt: {0} Forza Motorsport has native Trueforce, so also enable the plugin for it at the top of this panel.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGameNoteIRacing: Applies to iRacing. Turn iRacing's own force feedback OFF (do not set its strength to 0, the plugin reads that number), and set loadTrueForceAPI=0 in app.ini.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGameNoteLmu: Applies to Le Mans Ultimate. Checked, the wheel is driven from the sim's own steering shaft torque read straight from its shared memory, instead of the USB capture. In the game, set Vendor Specific Force Feedback to Off and Use LEDs off; its force feedback strength can stay. Unchecked returns to the USB capture (the tap route).
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGameNoteR3E: Applies to RaceRoom. Checked, the wheel is driven from the sim's own steering force read straight from its shared memory, instead of the USB capture. Unchecked returns to the USB capture (the tap route).
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGripCal_Tip: Shapes both the grip limit and the braking fade to each car's measured grip as you brake or slide, instead of one fixed point. Off also restores the classic lockup fade.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBGripLimitRowWhereTheGa: Where the game's combined-slip metric counts as the grip limit (1.0 = Forza's own limit). Lower = the wheel peaks and washes out earlier.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBIntro: The wheel's steering force is built from telemetry instead of the game's own FFB. Works in Forza Motorsport (2023) and Forza Horizon 4, 5, and 6. Set the game's force feedback and vibration to 0 so this is the only force on the wheel. Farming Simulator 22 and 25 are supported too, through the spring option below.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBIntroReshape_Fmt: The plugin takes force feedback over from {0} rather than inventing its own: it reads the forces the sim computes and delivers them over Trueforce, so the car still feels like the car and your rev lights and wheel screen work again. The setup steps are in the note below.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBIntroSpring: In Farming Simulator the plugin replaces the game's basic force feedback with its own steering model built from the game's physics, and engages by itself. The game's force feedback setting doesn't change the feel while SimHub runs; leaving it on just keeps native FFB as a fallback when SimHub is closed.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBIntroSpring_Tip: Also works in Forza Motorsport (2023) and Forza Horizon 4, 5, and 6.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBIntroWhatTelemetryBase: What Telemetry Based FFB does, and what to set in the game first.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBLateralDemand_Tip: Bases the steering force on cornering (lateral) grip instead of total grip.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBMinForce_Tip: Raising it lifts faint cues above the wheel's own friction and brings the average force up, so a belt-driven wheel like the G923 feels stronger overall.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBOled: Show telemetry on the wheel's screen
TelemetryFfb_ModeBRelearn_Tip: Forget what this car has learned and start again. Use it after a tune or a tire change makes the wheel feel wrong. This also clears the car's learned grip calibration.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBReset_Tip: Put the force tuning on this tab back to its defaults, including spike reduction.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBRevLights: Add rev light support to games when possible
TelemetryFfb_ModeBRevLights_Tip: The plugin works out per game and per session whether it can take the lights over without cutting the game's force feedback. Tick this to let it, whenever it can.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBSlipStarvedSetup_Tip: Jump to the Forza telemetry setup.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBSlipStarvedWarningTele: Telemetry Based FFB is on, but the game's telemetry is not reaching this plugin. In the game's Data Out settings, send telemetry to the plugin's port, then enable forwarding to SimHub. The Set up button shows the steps.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBSupportedLeaveSmoothin: Leave smoothing at 0 unless the wheel feels notchy or grainy.
TelemetryFfb_ModeBSupportedSmoothingMs_T: Smooths the force before it reaches the wheel. Higher = smoother feel but more lag; lower = tighter response. 0 = none, the default.
TelemetryFfb_NoRevLedMode_Tip: For the games that report no engine speed at all, like emulated arcade cabinets, where the rev lights have nothing to show.
TelemetryFfb_OledCustomPickALayoutThenWh: Pick a layout, then what goes in each of its slots. Anything set to Custom text shows exactly what you type.
TelemetryFfb_OledFlashStyle_Tip: The wheel cannot center its biggest text, so the large gear sits to one side with the speed next to it. The centered one is a size smaller but sits in the middle with a label.
TelemetryFfb_OledGreeting: Say hello when the screen first comes up
TelemetryFfb_OledGreetingText_Tip: Scrolls across the lower row under the plugin name. Anything longer than the row scrolls past.
TelemetryFfb_OledGreeting_Tip: Once each time SimHub runs, not once per session.
TelemetryFfb_OledLapResult: Show the lap when I cross the line
TelemetryFfb_OledLapResult_Tip: A personal best gets the time on its own. Any other lap gets the time with the delta under it.
TelemetryFfb_OledLayout_Tip: The wheel decides how big each slot is drawn and where it sits, so the layout is the shape and the slots are the contents.
TelemetryFfb_OledMph_Tip: Show the speed in mph instead of km/h. Affects this screen only.
TelemetryFfb_OledNoScreen: The wheel keeps its own display while you drive. Shifts, finished laps, incidents and warnings still take the screen for a moment and hand it straight back.
TelemetryFfb_OledPreviewHeldBack: preview held back: telemetry is arriving, so a game may be sending its own force feedback and writing the screen now could cut it. Close the game, or turn on Telemetry Based FFB, and the preview works.
TelemetryFfb_OledSectionItAlsoReportsCha: It also reports changes as they happen: a preset loading, a gain nudged from a bound button, Auto strength settling on a car, or a warning that the game is still sending its own force feedback. Each shows for a moment, then your driving screen comes back.
TelemetryFfb_OledSectionPutsYourSpeedGea: Puts your speed, gear, lap delta, and more on the little screen in the middle of the wheel, so you can read them without looking away from the road.
TelemetryFfb_OledShiftFlash: Flash the gear when I shift
TelemetryFfb_OledShiftFlash_Tip: Shows the gear for a moment on each shift. Skipped automatically on a screen that already shows the gear.
TelemetryFfb_OledTestOpenFailed: could not open the OLED channel (see log)
TelemetryFfb_R3EApplyStrength_Tip: Take what the plugin has watched this car push and use it as the car's max. The number on the button is that value. Greyed until the reading has held steady.
TelemetryFfb_R3EAutoStrength: Nudge it down to make this car feel heavier, up to make it lighter. Or drive and press Apply to set it from what the car pushes. Use Strength below for overall weight.
TelemetryFfb_R3EAutoStrengthRowCarSMax_T: The force level this car peaks at, on a 0 to 1 scale. Lower it to make this car lean harder on the wheel; raise it to make it lighter. Apply fills it from what the plugin has watched this car push.
TelemetryFfb_R3EDamperFade_Tip: The car speed at which the stationary friction has faded to nothing.
TelemetryFfb_R3EDamperStrength_Tip: How firm the parked resistance is. Higher is heavier; too high can start to shake, so it tops out where it stays smooth.
TelemetryFfb_R3EMaxDown_Tip: Lower this car's max a step, so it leans harder on the wheel.
TelemetryFfb_R3EMaxUp_Tip: Raise this car's max a step, so it feels lighter.
TelemetryFfb_R3EMax_Tip: The force level this car peaks at, on a 0 to 1 scale. Lower it to make this car lean harder on the wheel; raise it to make it lighter.
TelemetryFfb_R3EStationaryDamperFadesOut: The car speed at which the stationary friction has faded to nothing. Below it the friction eases off as you speed up; above it, only the sim's own force remains.
TelemetryFfb_R3EStationaryDamperFirmWhen: Firm when parked, easing off as you gain speed and gone by this speed (km/h).
TelemetryFfb_R3EStationaryDamperFriction: How firm the parked resistance is, as a share of full wheel force.
TelemetryFfb_R3EStationaryDamper_Tip: Adds back the game's low-speed parking resistance, which the handed-over, Telemetry Based and Farming Simulator routes otherwise drop. Firm when parked, fading to nothing as you gain speed.
TelemetryFfb_RestoresTheDefaultsFor: Restores the defaults for the game you are in, plus spike reduction, and leaves your other games alone.
TelemetryFfb_RevLightEffect_Tip: Colors and direction come from the pattern itself, set in G HUB.
TelemetryFfb_RevLightPattern: Picking a pattern sets the wheelbase's selection, like using the wheel's own menu: it applies now and stays. Remember for this car re-applies it whenever that car loads.
TelemetryFfb_SpikePeakRowsHoldsTheRunnin: Holds the running average up to at least this much, so ordinary force on a smooth road is not mistaken for a hit. It is also where a hit starts being slowed. Set it below normal road feel and everyday bumps start getting flattened and slowed.
TelemetryFfb_SpikePeakRowsTheMostAHitMay: The most a hit may rise above that running average. However hard the game hits, that is where it levels off, so a curb strike mid-corner lands this much above the corner instead of wrenching the wheel.
TelemetryFfb_SpikeTamingBodyMethod_Tip: The method picked below only applies while the box above is checked.
TelemetryFfb_SpikeTamingBodySomeGamesDel: Some games deliver curb and collision FFB spikes well beyond what's safe or comfortable on stronger wheelbases (Assetto Corsa is the worst offender we've seen). Hits can be sharp enough to wrench the wheel against your grip or strain your wrists on a long session.
TelemetryFfb_SpikeTamingEnabled: FFB spike reduction (recommended for Assetto Corsa)
TelemetryFfb_SpringCenterGain_Tip: 0 turns the spring off entirely, so you can feel what remains (terrain, damping, effects).
TelemetryFfb_SpringDrag_Tip: The steering grows heavier while your equipment is actually working the ground, a plow at depth pulls the wheel down, an empty run stays light. Plain engine strain (hard throttle, hills, hauling) adds a smaller touch of the same weight.
TelemetryFfb_SpringEssentialsOverallStee: Overall steering force (spring, terrain, drag, cornering weight together).
TelemetryFfb_SpringEssentialsTheSmallest: The smallest force your wheel actually plays here: lifts faint terrain hits, and light centering once the wheel is off dead-ahead, above the wheel's own friction. Raise it on a belt-driven wheel (G923) until faint bumps just move the wheel. A parked wheel stays limp, and damping is unaffected.
TelemetryFfb_SpringStrength_Tip: Damping is unaffected. The bound strength buttons adjust this while in Farming Simulator.
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrainBumpsAndGround: Bumps and ground texture reach the wheel as steering force. Needs the TF4ALL Enhanced Telemetry mod in the game (the plugin offers to install it).
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrainHowHardTheGrou: How hard the ground hits back.
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrainHowMuchCorneri: How much cornering load weighs the wheel.
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrainHowMuchOfThatW: How much of that weight plain engine strain applies with nothing working: hard throttle, hills, heavy hauling. 0 = implements only, 1 = strain counts in full.
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrainHowMuchSpeedSt: How much speed strengthens the centering. 0 = the same at every speed; 1 = fully speed-scaled with a limp standstill.
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrainHowMuchWorking: How much working equipment weighs the wheel.
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrainHowSolidTheWhe: How solid the wheel feels right at center. Higher = crisper straight-line feel without heavier edges.
TelemetryFfb_SpringTerrain_Tip: On by default. Field texture, ruts, and edges reach the wheel as steering force, not just the spring's centering.
TelemetryFfb_SpringWeight_Tip: The wheel loads up through turns based on how hard the vehicle is actually yawing. Most noticeable at road speeds.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringInertArcade: not used on an arcade cabinet
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringInertForzaC: not used in Forza on the capture route

Skipped in Forza on the capture route, where it can fight the game's own force feedback around pauses and drag the wheel hard to one side. Available with Telemetry Based FFB on. Your tuning still applies in other games.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringInertFricti: With RaceRoom's force handed over, the spring works against the plugin's own stationary friction instead of the game's parked damper. With that friction off there is nothing to settle the spring, so it is skipped. Turn the stationary friction on in the RaceRoom section to use it.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringInertIRacin: iRacing weights the wheel itself while parked, so the spring is skipped there. Your tuning still applies in other games.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringInertLocked: off outside Assetto Corsa, RaceRoom, Le Mans Ultimate and Forza in this version

The spring is offered in Assetto Corsa, RaceRoom, Le Mans Ultimate and Forza (with Telemetry Based FFB) in this version while it is retested game by game. Type SPRING in the access code box to unlock it for testing. Your saved per-game tuning is kept.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringInertOther_: Not used for the active game. Your tuning still applies in other games.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringSlidersFade: The spring is at full strength when stopped and fades to nothing by this speed. Keep it low so it's gone before real cornering forces build.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringSlidersSpri: How much centering weight to add when fully parked, as a fraction of full FFB. Start low; a strong spring can snap the wheel to center hard.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpringUnsupported: Skipped in Forza, where it can fight the game's own force feedback around pauses and drag the wheel hard to one side. Your tuning still applies in other games.
TelemetryFfb_StationarySpring_Tip: A parked car sends almost no force feedback, so the wheel feels limp. This adds a centering weight that fades out as you start moving and never fights the game's own FFB. It is set per game and off until you tick it, in Assetto Corsa, RaceRoom, Le Mans Ultimate or Forza with Telemetry Based FFB. Ignored for iRacing (the sim already weights the wheel).
TelemetryFfb_WheelLightsBlockColorsComeF: Colors come from the pattern above. Your revs always win in a game that reports them.
TelemetryFfb_WheelLightsBlockWhenAGameHa: When a game has no revs:
TelemetryFfb_WheelLightsBlockWhyTheLight: Why the lights work in some games and not others.

Welcome_AchievementsBody: Earn achievements for things like sharing presets, confirming car data, and supporting the project. Link your Discord account to get a matching role in the community server.
Welcome_CarDataBody: Effects like the engine pulse and rev limiter feel best when they know a car's engine and redline. Games don't always report that data in telemetry, and a few don't even give the car a real name, just a code like "car_123". Now, drivers can fill in the gaps, building a shared pool everyone benefits from. Saved per tune, so a swapped engine keeps its own redline.
Welcome_GrowsBody: The more drivers take part, the more often the right setup is already waiting when you load in. What you add helps the next person the same way.
Welcome_GrowsTitle: It gets better as it grows
Welcome_Heading: Introducing: community presets and car data
Welcome_Intro: This update adds a community preset browser, crowd-sourced car data, and per-car corrections. Community features are on: car data you tune (redlines, engine types, car names) is shared anonymously and improves everyone's defaults. You can turn any of this off in Settings. An account is only needed for the preset browser (free email sign-in).
Welcome_PresetsBody: Browse and download presets other drivers have shared, for the car you're driving or the game you're playing. Vote on the ones you've tried so the best rise to the top.
Welcome_PrivacyBody: Car data you contribute is anonymous. Sign-in (only needed for presets) takes just your email and a one-time code. No password, no signup form. The privacy policy spells out what's stored and how to remove it.
Welcome_TestBackendBody: The community backend is still in testing. Shared presets and packs here are test data and may be reset before the public launch. Your account, achievements, and any car data you contribute are kept.
